𝐁𝐎𝐂 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬 ₱𝟐𝟎𝟎𝐌 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐡 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐨𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐨 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐬, 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐮𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬, 𝐑𝐚𝐰 𝐌𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐂𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐝

The Bureau of Customs (BOC), together  with the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine National Police (PNP), and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), uncovered an estimated ₱200 million worth of illicit cigarette manufacturing equipment, raw materials, and finished products in a joint inter-agency operation aimed at dismantling large-scale violations of customs and economic sabotage laws.

The operation was carried out pursuant to Letter of Authority No. 02-18-023-2026 and Mission Order No. 02-18-028-2026, following intelligence information indicating possible violations of Republic Act No. 10863, or the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA), and Republic Act No. 12022, otherwise known as the Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act.

The joint operation was led by the BOC Intelligence Group, through the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Service (CIIS), and was supported by elements of the AFP Intelligence Units, PNP-CALABARZON, Criminal Investigation and Detection Group - Cavite, the Bureau of Fire Protection-Tanza, and the Local Government Unit of Tanza.

Initial information indicated that the warehouse had previously been used for the storage of canned goods. However, reports from a concerned citizen regarding a strong tobacco odor inconsistent with the declared use of the facility prompted surveillance, validation, and subsequent enforcement action.

The BOC, in coordination with other operating units, exercised its visitorial powers over the subject warehouse. The inspection yielded positive results, leading to the discovery of equipment, raw materials, and finished products suspected to be used in the manufacture, storage, and distribution of smuggled and counterfeit cigarettes.

Based on the initial assessment conducted by the BOC, the seized items include eleven (11) suspected cigarette manufacturing machines, two (2) generator sets, one (1) forklift, and ten (10) brands of finished cigarette products. Among the cigarette brands initially identified were Champion, Marlboro, Canon Menthol, New Orleans, Bros, New Berlin, Commando, Delta, and Troy, subject to final inventory and verification.

Authorities also discovered fake and irregular tax stamps, reinforcing suspicions of large-scale illicit cigarette production and distribution intended to evade lawful duties and taxes.

The combined value of the seized machinery, raw materials, and finished cigarette products is initially estimated at ₱200 million, subject to final assessment and inventory by the BOC.

The BOC emphasized that the operation underscores the government’s intensified campaign against smuggling, illicit manufacturing, and economic sabotage—particularly activities that undermine legitimate industries, deprive the government of lawful revenues, and harm Filipino farmers—consistent with the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
